summary: This component renders a blog post item that adapts its display based on whether the user is viewing a single post or browsing a list of posts. It conditionally shows certain UI elements like an AI icon, copy-to-markdown button, and engagement features only when viewing the full post, while always showing the core post content and header/footer.

explanations.22: This helper function checks if we're on the actual blog post page versus a list view, and returns a CSS class name to add bottom spacing only in list view.
explanations.23: useBlogPost is a Docusaurus hook that gives us metadata about the current blog context, including whether we're viewing a single post or a list.
explanations.28: We're extracting both the blog post metadata and the isBlogPostPage flag from the Docusaurus hook so we can use them throughout this component.
explanations.29: frontMatter contains custom metadata fields defined in the blog post's YAML header, like whether it was AI-assisted.
explanations.31: This shows the AI icon only if two conditions are true: the post is marked as AI-assisted AND we're on the actual post page (not a list card).
explanations.34: The copy-as-markdown button only appears on the full post page, not on list view cards, because copying wouldn't make sense in a list context.
explanations.44: Everything inside this block only renders when viewing the actual post page, not when the post appears as a card in the blog list.
explanations.57: This checks that tried_it is not explicitly false before showing the TriedIt component, meaning it displays by default unless the post author disabled it.
